answer_raw:
Finding the cheapest two-week winter trip depends on whether you prioritize low transit costs or low local living costs, as the cheapest flight destinations from the U.S. in 2026 don't always align with the lowest cost of living.

The available sources do not provide specific pricing for two-week travel packages or a breakdown of flight vs. living costs for specific winter destinations. To get a complete picture, you would need to cross-reference flight search engines with cost-of-living tools like Numbeo.

## Strategic Options

**Low-cost flight focus**
If you want to minimize the initial hit to your budget, look for the 10 cheapest destinations to fly to from the U.S. in 2026, which were identified via research on thousands of flight routes and millions of bookings as of Jan 15, 2026 [3]. While these are the cheapest to reach, you must verify if the local cost of living in those specific cities allows for a two-week stay without exceeding your budget.

**Short-haul/Regional focus**
If you want to avoid long-haul flight costs entirely, you can look at escapes within a 3-hour drive from NYC, such as the Catskills or Rhode Island, as of Nov 24, 2025 [1]. While these have lower transit costs, the "living costs" (hotels/rentals) during the winter season may be higher than a budget-friendly international destination.

**Warm-weather seasonal shifts**
A common practical solution for New Yorkers seeking warmth is flying to places like Boca, Florida. Because all three major NYC airports (JFK, LGA, EWR) have dozens of daily flights to these hubs, prices remain competitive [6]. 

## Comparison Framework

| Strategy | Transit Cost | Living Cost | Best For |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Domestic/Regional** | Low (driving or short flight) | Likely higher per night [1] | Minimizing travel time |
| **Top 10 US Flight Targets** | Lowest (per 2026 research) [3] | Variable | Maximizing flight budget |
| **Warm-weather Hubs** | Competitive (via JFK/LGA/EWR) [6] | Likely higher seasonally [6] | Climate/warmth preference |
